core_obligations: Note that the statement makes sense because the completion is adic* and hence the notion of an adic morphism applies, and that such a morphism is representable (proof lines 7323-7327).

Apply the comparison of morphisms from the spectrum and the formal spectrum of a complete local Noetherian algebra to obtain a unique morphism g into X lifting the composition of the given morphism with the comparison map (proof lines 7327-7331).

Show that the fibre product of the formal spectrum with the reduced induced structure on T is an algebraic space with a closed immersion into the formal spectrum, and that it agrees with the corresponding fibre product over X because the comparison map is a monomorphism (proof lines 7331-7340).

Deduce that this fibre product is the spectrum of a quotient by an ideal containing a power of the maximal ideal, identify the corresponding fibre product over the spectrum of R with the quotient by another ideal, and use that the two agree after passing to every sufficiently high quotient to conclude by Krull's intersection theorem (proof lines 7340-7351).
proof_roadmap: The statement makes sense: adic* completion and representability (proof lines 7323-7327).
Lifting the morphism to the ambient space (proof lines 7327-7331).
The fibre product with the reduced closed subspace (proof lines 7331-7340).
Comparing two ideals and applying Krull's intersection theorem (proof lines 7340-7351).
difficulty_reason: For an algebraic space X with a closed subset T whose complement is quasi-compact, and a complete local Noetherian algebra R, the lemma asserts that an adic morphism from the formal spectrum of R into the formal completion of X along T corresponds to a unique morphism from the spectrum of R into X whose preimage of T is exactly the closed point (statement lines 7314-7321). That the statement makes sense uses that the completion is adic* by an earlier result on the types of formal completions, so that adicness of morphisms is available (proof lines 7323-7326). The proof first applies the statement comparing morphisms from the spectrum and from the formal spectrum of a complete local Noetherian ring to produce a unique morphism g into X lifting the composition of the given adic morphism with the comparison map (proof lines 7327-7330). It then studies the fibre product of the formal spectrum with the reduced induced structure on T: since the given morphism is adic it is representable, the fibre product is an algebraic space with a closed immersion into the formal spectrum, and because the comparison map is a monomorphism this fibre product can also be computed over X (proof lines 7331-7340). It is therefore the spectrum of a quotient of R by an ideal containing a power of the maximal ideal, and comparing that quotient with the fibre product of the spectrum of R with the reduced subspace over successive thickenings gives two ideals with the same images modulo every sufficiently high power of the maximal ideal; Krull's intersection theorem then forces the two ideals to be equal, which is exactly the assertion about the preimage of T (proof lines 7340-7351). The claim is H2: the argument combines a lifting statement with a computation of two fibre products and closes it by an intersection theorem, each step named and displayed.
